summary: Tested the client-side image enhance feature (front and back), how it combines with trim and clear-bg, PDF/PNG/JPG export after enhancing, PDF export of bomboniera tags at 600dpi (hires) and regressions. Backend: 24/24 pytest pass (18 old + 6 new hires tests). Frontend: every requested flow works with no page errors.
verified: 600x400 -> enhance -> toast 'Immagine migliorata (1800×1200px)', info 1800×1200px, preview src changed, button pink + title 'Annulla miglioramento'; second click restores 600×400 and original src
Max 3x cap: 500x500 -> 1500x1500; back image 300x200 -> 900x600 (item-0-back-enhance) with undo working
Enhance then trim -> 1203×723 (the rest of the image stays correct); clear-bg afterwards shows the info toast 'Nessuno sfondo...' with no errors
Export after enhance: PDF, PNG and multi-image JPG download; duplex PDF with front and back enhanced downloads
Tag mode + back text -> PDF has 2 pages, embedded images 2126x591 = 9x2.5cm @600dpi
Backend: hires=true at dpi150 embeds 2008x1299 (600dpi) vs 502x325 without hires; hires is ignored for png; the default is false
critical_code_review_comments: The item DPI indicator (e.g. '179 DPI') jumps to ~538 after the upscale enhance. This can mislead users into thinking the image has real print resolution. Consider computing the DPI from the original pixels, or adding a label such as 'interpolata'.
enhanceImage always encodes to PNG. A 2400px photo can become a 5-15MB upload, so consider JPEG at quality 0.92 for opaque images.
Enhance steps stack: enhance -> trim -> enhance again re-enhances an already enhanced image, so sharpening and contrast build up. Undo only goes back one step, which is acceptable.
URL.createObjectURL is never revoked when images are replaced, so memory slowly leaks during long sessions (minor).
The TileCache key does not include dpi/hires. This is safe today because the key uses id(img) per item, but it is fragile.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Test images are generated with PIL into /tmp/imgs. The enhance testids are item-N-front-enhance and item-N-back-enhance. The back text textarea is item-0-back-txt-textarea (tag mode). The template name input only appears in tag mode, so it was not tested this iteration (it was covered in iteration_5).
